idiom_name: final class conforming to the protocol, backed by a Dictionary
implementation_notes: The collaborator is a protocol and the fake is a small conforming type whose store is a Dictionary - the ordinary way to write an implementation in Swift, with no framework or code generation involved, and protocol extensions can supply the members a given test does not care about. Use a final class when the code under test stores the collaborator, and a struct when the fake is only used within one test function, because value semantics then prevent accidental sharing. Keep the fake in the test target, and keep one test against the real implementation to catch protocol drift.
pitfalls: A struct fake is copied when installed: the code under test mutates its own copy and the test's copy never sees the writes - use a final class when the collaborator is stored, or pass the fake inout.
A reference-semantics fake kept in a shared fixture leaks state between tests; re-create it per test.
Under strict concurrency a fake captured by an async collaborator must be Sendable (or @unchecked with internal locking), otherwise the compiler rejects the test or the data races.
